newsitem.title: BELGIUM: UK secures victory on EMU legal pact-Clarke.
newsitem.headline: UK secures victory on EMU legal pact-Clarke.

text.p: Britain has won a change in a proposed European Union regulation that defines the legal framework for a single currency, Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Monday.
Under the regulation, countries that do not participate in the single currency will not now be under any obligation to abide by its legal parameters.
"We wanted to make it crystal clear that this does not apply to those who opt out," Clarke told reporters. "We got it without any particular difficulty."
The proposed regulation would come into force once countries are chosen to enter monetary union in 1999.
EU finance ministers have proposed bringing forward legislation on a number of issues concerning the single currency, such as the continuity of contracts, under Article 235 of the Maastricht treaty.
This will allow them next year to meet some of the concerns of the financial markets concerning the legality of the new currency, the Euro.
But other legal issues were due to be agreed under another article -- 109L4 -- that takes effect when the EU fixes its exchange rates for the currency.
Clarke's amendment says countries that have opted out of the currency will not have to abide by legal rules imposed under 109L4. -- Brussels newsroom 32 2 287 6830
